first-390.help: How the Season Center worksYour season was played the moment you pressed the button. This is that same season, game by game, so nothing here can change it. Your career is the same whether you watch or not.The teams, the divisions and how often you meet each one follow the league's standard schedule formula. How the games are grouped into series, which series falls where and which park a league series is played in, every score and every stat line are this career's own, not a real schedule.Your team's record is this career's own too. It always fits how your season ended: here a champion wins 92 to 108 of 162 and a team that missed the playoffs 52 to 86.If a contract talk comes up when you press Week by week, answer it first. If you play the year out, the season runs straight away and you can open it afterwards with Watch again.▶ plays the next game. ⏩ jumps to the next big one (halfway, the last game). ⏭ goes straight to the end. 1x and 3x set the clock, Results shows each game at the final.Worked examplesA gameGame 41, at home to the Atlanta Braves. You win 6-4 and go 2 for 4 with a home run and 3 RBI. Your record goes to 24-17.Your numbersYour season card says .287 with 24 home runs and 81 RBI. Every home run, RBI, double and steal here adds up to exactly that, and your hits over your at bats round to .287. Walks are not dealt game by game, so your on base percentage is the one on your card.SeriesBaseball is played in series: a few games in a row against one club in one park. You meet each division rival 13 times, and how often you meet everybody else follows the league formula too. A game you sat out reads Did not play.The inningsThe clock runs inning by inning. Each line is the runs a side put up in that inning, and a home run of yours is called out in the inning it came in. A game still level after nine is settled in extra innings, shown as one last mark.All-StarIf your season card has an All-Star on it, the halfway point tells you so.The playoffs show as a path, round by round, with the numbers your season card already has. From 2026 on, the league is this career's own world on today's format. Every October here starts at the first round: this career has no first round bye. The path shows each round and its score, not who you played. A season before 2022 shows no playoff path, because the playoffs had a different shape then, and a season whose playoff games do not fit today's rounds shows none either.Got it
